newsitem.title: UK: RBA's Macfarlane looking for pickup in 1997/8.
newsitem.headline: RBA's Macfarlane looking for pickup in 1997/8.

text.p: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) governor Ian Macfarlane said on Thursday the Australian economy looked set for a pickup in growth in 1997-98.

But Macfarlane, speaking at a banking seminar in London, also said there was considerable spare capacity in the economy and that the central bank's aim was for a sustained period of low inflation growth.
"We are looking for some pickup in growth in 1997/1998," he said.
He said that unlike in the U.S., Australia still had considerable spare capacity in its economy.
He said the aim of the RBA was to have a prolonged period of sustained low inflation growth, and the way a central bank can do this was to keep inflation under control.

Macfarlane said that was the logic behind the government's inflation target which formally says inflation should be kept between two and three percent, and informally meant the reserve bank wanted it to average "two point something".
He said that this system was working well, and combined with an independent central bank would allow inflation to be maintained.
Macfarlane also said the RBA wanted to keep the current expansion going longer than in previous periods of growth, which were around six and a half years.
